subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Alternating Current: The Wave
description: A 60-second lesson on Alternating Current: The Wave.

hook.text: Your wall outlet delivers current that reverses direction 50 or 60 times per second.

buildup.text: AC voltage rises, peaks, falls to zero, goes negative, then repeats.

discovery.text: Transformers only work with AC. They step voltage up or down effortlessly.

twist.text: High voltage AC travels hundreds of miles with minimal loss. DC couldn't do that in 1890.

climax.text: Tesla and Westinghouse won the current war. AC powers the world's grid.

punchline.text: AC won because transformers make long-distance power cheap.

quiz.question: Why did AC win the 'war of currents' for power grids?
options: AC is safer than DC at all voltages
Transformers can easily change AC voltage for efficient long-distance transmission
AC uses less copper wire than DC
